hook_text: Draw it in Johannesburg, post it to Cape Town, get back a perfect steel part. Here is the code that makes that work.
clip_script: A drawing office in Germiston draws a bracket. The drawing goes to a workshop in Cape Town. Back comes a perfect part. How? A shared language of lines and numbers. Lines first. Dark solid: edges you can see. Faint: your guide lines, left on lightly. Dashed: edges that are hidden, like a hole seen from the side. Dash-dot: centre lines through holes and rods. Then scale. 1:2 is half size, so a 300 millimetre frame is drawn 150. But here is the trick: you still write 300, because the number on the drawing is always the real size. Then dimensions. Millimetres, no unit. Two thin lines out from the ends, a thin line between with arrowheads, the number above. Outside the drawing, each size once, overall sizes always. Learn the code and anyone anywhere can build what you draw.
visual_style: A whiteboard rectangle gains its four line types one by one, shrinks under a 1:2 label while the written 300 stays, then grows projection lines, arrowheads and figures.
pacing: Lines in twenty seconds, scale in fifteen, dimensions in twenty, one-line close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and dimension a 300 by 20 mm upright with a hole 15 mm from the top.
